subject.title: skill safe-encryption-skill: Spec Prohibits File Output But CLI Tool's Standard Interface Is File Output

question: Should ClawHub leave v0.1.0 listed while requesting a publisher correction, or hide or revoke it until its encryption-output guardrails are internally consistent?
rationale: Current code offers both non-blocking publisher/report workflows and restrictive moderation tools, but repository evidence cannot determine the acceptable security threshold for this live third-party package.

options.title: Request corrected release
options.body: Ask the publisher to add verified stdin/stdout syntax and distinguish permitted final ciphertext from prohibited temporary intermediates while leaving the listing visible.

options.title: Hide pending correction
options.body: Use report triage or staff moderation to hide the skill until a corrected version replaces v0.1.0.

options.title: Revoke v0.1.0
options.body: Revoke the exact version, which should hide the skill when no earlier public version remains, and restore availability through a corrected release.

recommendation.title: Request corrected release
recommendation.body: Ask the publisher to add verified stdin/stdout syntax and distinguish permitted final ciphertext from prohibited temporary intermediates while leaving the listing visible.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this contributor most directly to the exact-version deletion, scanning, and moderation lifecycle needed to implement the registry-side decision.
